title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook — SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the standard approach for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site procedures, and the canonical fixes for the top support issues. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and maintainable docs that reduce support load, accelerate user onboarding, and make code examples reliable across releases.

Scope

Applies to all public and internal DevEx artifacts in the eng-developer-experience space, including: SDK reference guides (Python, JS, Go), quickstarts, example apps, API snippet library, and docs-site procedures and CI pipelines.

Owner and Review Process

- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience documentation team
- Document author: individual contributor or PM responsible for a feature/SDK
- Reviewers: at least 2 reviewers (one SDK owner + one product or platform reviewer)
- Approval: doc must be approved in PR in docs repo and proofread for accuracy (examples run successfully)

Required Metadata for Every Doc (enforced by templates)

1. title 
2. summary (one-sentence)
3. author + owner_team
4. status (draft | in_review | published)
5. created_at, last_updated
6. reviewers (>=1)
7. labels (>=1)
8. related_pages (optional)

File Naming and Location Conventions

- Filenames: short, descriptive, dash-separated, end with year when appropriate. Examples: "sdk-python-auth-quickstart-2026.json"
- Location: place SDK guides under eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides or quickstarts under eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Versioning: include major version in filename for breaking changes (e.g., v2)

Template: SDK Guide Structure

Every SDK guide must follow this structure (copyable template in repo):

1) Title and short summary
2) Quickstart (1–3 minute) — minimal code to get started
3) Installation and requirements
4) Auth and config (environment variables, KMS notes if relevant)
5) Full examples (sync/async patterns, streaming, error handling)
6) Common support issues and FAQ (link back to central top-issues doc)
7) API reference links and compatibility matrix
8) Changelog and migration notes

Example: Python Quickstart (minimal)

```python
# Install: pip install redwood-sdk
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-alpha-1", prompt="Write a short haiku about devex")
print(resp.text)
```

CLI Quickstart (cURL)

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"Hello from curl"}'

SDK Guidelines (best practices)

- Keep quickstarts < 30 lines and runnable
- Prefer typed examples (Python typing / TypeScript)
- Use real, small outputs in examples (not truncated ellipses)
- Include both minimal and production examples (retries, backoff, idempotency keys)
- Mark breaking changes in header and include migration snippet

Quickstarts & Templates Catalog (examples)

- app-quickstart-rest: small Flask + SDK app showing text generation and streaming
- embeddings-search-template: minimal indexer + similarity search using Redwood embeddings
- function-calling-example: shows structured output + tool-calling pattern
- rate-limit-handling: template for exponential backoff and circuit breaker

Quickstart Template (checklist)

- Title and TL;DR
- Prereqs: SDK version, Python/Node version, env vars
- Setup steps (numbered)
- Run and expected output section (exact output snapshot)
- Cleanup steps
- Troubleshooting section with at least 3 known failure modes and commands to collect logs

Config Table Example (use this structure in docs)

| Parameter | Default | Description | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | - | API key for calls | devex | Required for all examples |
| SDK_VERSION | latest | pinned SDK version for quickstart | devex | update on release |
| NODE_VERSION | 18.x | Node runtime used in examples | devex | test via CI |

API Examples Library

Centralize snippet ownership in repo: docs/snippets/. Each snippet must be tagged by language, API surface, and test-case filename. Snippet format: executable file + metadata JSON (tags, version, expected_output).

Example: Text generation (Node)

```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-alpha-1', prompt: 'Summarize the Redwood mission in one sentence.' });
console.log(res.text);
```

Error handling and retries (canonical)

- Use per-request idempotency keys for operations that must not duplicate effects.
- Retry on 429, 503 using exponential backoff (jitter). Do NOT retry on 400 or 401.
- Circuit breaker recommended for high-volume batch jobs (example template in snippets/circuit-breaker.js).

Docs Site Operating Procedures

- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs
- Branching: trunk-based docs workflow (feature branches -> PR -> CI)
- CI checks (PR must pass): 
  - build (mkdocs or Hugo)
  - snippet tests (execute pinned examples inside isolated env)
  - link-check (no broken internal links)
  - spelling and linting
- Deploy: Automated on merge to main to https://docs.redwood.ai; emergency hotfixes go through release branch and require 2 approvers
- SLAs: docs build success rate SLO: 99% per week; broken-snippet alert TTL: 24 hours for owner team to triage

CI Commands (common)

- Local preview: make docs-serve (runs a local dev server at http://localhost:8000)
- Run snippet tests: ./scripts/run-snippet-tests.sh --language python,js
- Rebuild and deploy: git push && GitHub Actions releases deployment

Change and Deprecation Policy for Docs

1. For non-breaking updates: update doc, run CI, merge.
2. For breaking SDK/API changes: author publishes migration guide, updates quickstarts, and notifies customers via engineering-announce and changelog.
3. Deprecation window: 90 days for SDK-breaking changes with banner on affected docs and redirect to migration guide.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (DevEx-specific)

This section collects the most frequently opened support tickets related to developer docs and canonical fixes. Each entry contains: symptom, quick triage, root cause patterns, canonical fix, and owner.

1) SDK auth failures (most common)
- Symptom: 401 Unauthorized in SDK examples or cURL
- Quick triage: Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY set? echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY; try curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Root causes: env var not exported locally, key expired, using test key in prod region
- Canonical fix: Update quickstart to include export step, add health-check snippet, and a troubleshooting note on scopes. Owner: devex + platform-auth.

2) Example snippets fail after SDK release
- Symptom: CI snippet tests fail post-release
- Quick triage: Check pinned SDK_VERSION in snippet metadata; run failing snippet locally
- Root causes: API change, renamed parameter, model name change
- Canonical fix: Pin and run snippets in CI, bump snippets with release PR that updates examples and adds migration snippet. Owner: SDK team.

3) Streaming responses not handled correctly
- Symptom: empty buffer or partial JSON when streaming content
- Quick triage: Reproduce with local dev server, verify streaming client pattern (does it parse chunk boundaries?)
- Root causes: incorrect event parsing, missing backpressure handling in example
- Canonical fix: Provide recommended stream-consumer pattern per language (Node: use eventsource parser; Python: async iterator example). Owner: devex + runtime.

4) High-latency calls in quickstarts
- Symptom: sample app shows >2s response for generation
- Quick triage: Run request with X-Request-ID header and consult docs console traces, compare model variant
- Root causes: using large model by default in quickstart, no warmup or batching for demo
- Canonical fix: Set quickstarts to use low-latency model (redwood-alpha-lite), add note about expected p50/p95, include steps to run locally with smaller prompts. Owner: devex + runtime.

5) Mismatched expected output in tests
- Symptom: unit tests in quickstart assert exact output and fail intermittently
- Quick triage: Check whether tests rely on nondeterministic model output; switch to prompt that yields deterministic format (e.g., structured JSON with system prompt)
- Root causes: tests assert on natural language generation
- Canonical fix: Use structured output (function calling or JSON schema) for test assertions, mock responses in CI for deterministic runs. Owner: devex + qa.

6) Broken links after reorg
- Symptom: 404 when following internal link from quickstart to API reference
- Quick triage: run docs link-check CI job or manual check of path; open PR to fix target path
- Root causes: page moved without redirects, file rename not mirrored in links
- Canonical fix: Maintain redirects in docs config; add link-check CI gating. Owner: docs-ops.

7) Incorrect rate-limit guidance
- Symptom: customers hit 429s even when following published guidance
- Quick triage: verify published rate-limits vs. customer tier; check header X-RateLimit-Remaining on responses
- Root causes: guidance outdated, or example uses burst traffic pattern
- Canonical fix: Update docs with per-tenant SLOs, include sample backoff code, and add note on testing at scale. Owner: product + devex.

8) Embeddings indexing mismatch
- Symptom: similarity search returns unexpected results
- Quick triage: confirm embedding model version and vector dimension; run a local similarity check with known pairs
- Root causes: mixing embeddings from different models or failing to normalize vectors
- Canonical fix: Standardize embeddings model in quickstart, include dimension and normalization steps in template. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals + devex.

Triage Playbook (step-by-step for doc-related tickets)

1. Reproduce: run snippet locally using the same SDK version and environment variables described by user.
2. Isolate: if failing only in CI, collect logs (ci-run-id) and run snippet in an identical container image.
3. Patch: prepare a docs PR with fix; include updated snippet test and request reviewer from owning team.
4. Communicate: update support ticket with steps, ETA, and link to PR; if user-facing, create temporary workaround in ticket.

Measurement and Continuous Improvement

- Metrics to track: number of doc-related support tickets per month, snippet test pass rate, docs build success rate, time-to-fix for broken snippets
- Quarterly review: devex reviews top 10 support issues, updates quickstarts and examples, and runs a docs game-day to exercise snippet testing and CI recovery

Appendix: Useful Commands and Links

- Docs repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs.git
- Snippets folder: docs/snippets/
- Run local docs server: make docs-serve
- Run snippet tests: ./scripts/run-snippet-tests.sh --languages python,js
- Contact: #devex on Slack for reviewer requests; use @doc-owner handle for urgent fixes

Canonical Artifact Locations

- Quickstarts: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- SDK guides: confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides (create if missing)
- API examples: docs/snippets/ in GitHub repo

Notes

This playbook is periodically reviewed (quarterly) or when major SDK/runtime changes occur. For suggested edits, open a PR in the docs repo and tag @Aisha Patel and the relevant owner team.
